topic: The Neural Library: How MLPs in Transformers Store Facts
target_audience: University students in computer science or AI-enthusiasts with basic linear algebra knowledge

outline.topic: The Neural Library: How MLPs in Transformers Store Facts
outline.target_audience: University students in computer science or AI-enthusiasts with basic linear algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Mystery of the Knowledge Base
sections.content: Introduce the paradox: Transformers are known for processing sequences (Attention), but where is the 'encyclopedia' stored? Identify the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) blocks, which contain roughly 2/3 of a model's parameters, as the likely storage for factual knowledge.
sections.example: Imagine a robot named 'Lexi' who knows that 'Eiffel Tower' is in 'Paris'. While the Attention mechanism looks at the words around her, the MLP acts as her internal library card catalog.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Key-Value Memory Systems
sections.content: Explain the abstract concept of associative memory. A 'Key' is a pattern to look for, and a 'Value' is the information associated with it. Visualize this as a dictionary where looking up a word (Key) gives you a definition (Value).
sections.example: Think of a vending machine: The code 'A1' is the Key; the actual bag of chips released is the Value.

sections.title: Anatomy of an MLP: The Two-Step Mechanism
sections.content: Break down the MLP into two linear transformations with a non-linear activation (ReLU/GELU). Visually represent the first matrix (W1) as a set of 'Key' detectors and the second matrix (W2) as a set of 'Value' injectors. Mathematically, show y = f(x · W1) · W2.
sections.example: Visual: Matrix W1 is a wall of 'lock holes' (keys). Matrix W2 is a tray of 'prizes' (values). If the input vector 'fits' a lock in W1, the corresponding prize in W2 is pushed into the model's workflow.

sections.title: The Activation Trigger (The ReLU Gate)
sections.content: Explain the role of the non-linear activation function. If the input vector matches a 'Key' in W1, the neuron 'fires' (activates). If it doesn't match, the output is zero. This ensures only relevant facts are retrieved for the current context.
sections.example: Graphical: A line graph showing a 'threshold'. If the 'Eiffel Tower' signal is strong enough, the gate opens; if we are talking about 'Eiffel's blueprint', a different key might trigger.

sections.title: Information Injection into the Residual Stream
sections.content: Describe the 'Residual Stream' as a moving conveyor belt of information. The MLP doesn't replace the data; it adds a 'Knowledge Vector' to the stream. Show the vector addition: x_new = x_old + MLP(x_old).
sections.example: Visual: A boat (the word 'Paris') floating down a river. As it passes the MLP station, a crane drops a 'Capital of France' package onto the boat, making the information more complete.

sections.title: The Superposition: Storing Billions of Facts
sections.content: Address how so many facts fit. In high-dimensional space, vectors can be 'nearly orthogonal' (almost 90 degrees apart). This allows thousands of 'Keys' to exist in the same MLP layer without interfering with each other.
sections.example: Visual: A 3D sphere where thousands of pins (fact vectors) are stuck. Even though the sphere is small, the pins don't touch because there is so much 'space' in higher dimensions.

sections.title: Summary & Conclusion
sections.content: Recap the 5-minute journey: MLPs are not just math functions; they are associative memories. W1 recognizes the context (Key), and W2 provides the fact (Value). Together, they turn a sequence processor into a knowledgeable assistant.
sections.example: Lexi the Robot successfully answers 'Paris' because her MLP 'Key' for 'Capital of France' fired and injected the correct 'Value' into her thought stream.

storyboard.title: The Mystery of the Knowledge Base
lecture_lines: Where do Transformers store their massive encyclopedia of facts?
Attention handles sequences, but MLPs hold the knowledge.
Nearly two-thirds of parameters live within these MLP blocks.
animations: Lexi the robot appears with a thought bubble 'Eiffel Tower: Paris'.
Transformer diagram zooms into the MLP block, highlighting it in #FFD700.
Text 'MLPs store 2/3 of model parameters' appears clearly.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Key-Value Memory Systems
lecture_lines: Knowledge relies on a system of keys and values.
A key represents a specific pattern to recognize.
The value is the information associated with that pattern.
animations: 'Key' (#FF4500) and 'Value' (#1E90FF) labels appear over a dictionary icon.
Vending machine: input 'A1' (Key) results in 'Chips' (Value).
Graphic transforms: Key-Value pairs become rows in a Weight Matrix.

storyboard.title: Anatomy of an MLP: The Two-Step Mechanism
lecture_lines: Input vectors interact with the first matrix, W1.
W1 acts as a set of specific pattern detectors.
A non-linear activation determines if a pattern matches.
If matched, the second matrix, W2, provides information.
W2 injects a "value" vector back into the model.
animations: Centered formula: y = ReLU(x * W1) * W2 with W1 in #00FFFF and W2 in #FF00FF.
W1 matrix rows glow as they detect specific input patterns.
ReLU function graph appears; signals below zero are blocked.
W2 matrix columns represent knowledge vectors being retrieved.
Visual sum: Activation strength scales the retrieved Value vector.

storyboard.title: The Activation Trigger (The ReLU Gate)
lecture_lines: The activation function acts as a selective gate.
Only strong pattern matches trigger the factual retrieval.
Irrelevant information is filtered out by returning zero.
animations: Large ReLU graph shows y=0 for x<0 and y=x for x>0.
A 'firing' neuron flashes when the input signal exceeds the threshold.
Contrast: 'Eiffel Tower' triggers the gate; 'Eiffel Blueprint' does not.

storyboard.title: Information Injection into the Residual Stream
lecture_lines: Information travels along a path called the residual stream.
The MLP does not replace the existing data flow.
Instead, it adds new factual vectors to the stream.
This process is represented by simple vector addition.
Each layer enriches the context with more specific facts.
animations: Horizontal blue conveyor belt (#ADD8E6) labeled 'Residual Stream' moves right.
Data x is tapped from the stream into the MLP block.
MLP processes x and produces a 'Knowledge Vector' delta x.
The delta x vector is added (+) back onto the moving belt.
The combined information x + delta x continues down the stream.

storyboard.title: The Superposition: Storing Billions of Facts
lecture_lines: How can one layer store millions of distinct facts?
High-dimensional spaces provide an incredible amount of room.
Vectors can be nearly perpendicular to avoid interference.
This phenomenon is known as superposition in neural networks.
Thousands of keys coexist without overlapping or blurring.
animations: A large circle (#555555) appears on screen.
Two arrows at 90 degrees demonstrate orthogonality.
Dozens of new vectors (lines) are added to the circle.
Text overlay: 'High-dimensional space allows for nearly orthogonal vectors.'
The circle glows with thousands of distinct 'fact points'.

storyboard.title: Summary & Conclusion
lecture_lines: MLPs act as the internal library of the Transformer.
They recognize patterns and inject relevant factual data.
This turns a simple processor into a knowledgeable assistant.
animations: Summary graphic: W1 (Key Detector) + W2 (Value Injector).
Lexi the Robot correctly identifies Paris as the capital of France.
Credits/Ending text: 'MLPs: The Knowledge Engines of AI.'
